method.baseline: Record-only runs of scripts/probe-performance-budget.mts (server) and tests/performance/long-track-render.spec.ts (browser) on this machine, each sample stamped with os.loadavg()[0]. statisticValue is the worst per-run statistic across those runs.
method.budget: budget = baseline statisticValue x headroom factor, rounded up to two significant figures (never more than 10 % above the product). parseBudgetFile refuses a budget that does not follow from its baseline and factor.
method.statistic: Nearest-rank percentile over at least 20 samples per p95 metric (minimumSamples), so the p95 is the 19th of 20 and one outlier on the loaded machine does not decide it. Baseline runs with fewer samples stay in the record but do not set a p95 baseline. max metrics (memory, sizes, the heap ladder) take the worst sample.
method.flakeAvoidance: Budgets are judged only in separate opt-in steps (the probe; playwright.performance.config.ts), never in pnpm test or pnpm test:identity. Headroom is set on the loaded baseline, so an idle machine meets it with more margin. Admissible load (rule added in M2-01k-f round 4, after judged run 3 failed at a load average up to 124; no earlier version defined one): a time budget exceeded while any of its samples was taken above that metric's baseline.loadAverage1m.max is `inconclusive`, not failed, and the run is repeated at an admissible load. Load never turns a failure into a pass and never excuses memory or size metrics. evaluateBudget enforces this.
method.noArtificialLoad: No load generator was run. The engine load is product requests at the admission limits, bounded in count and duration.
method.graphBinding: M2-01ak: the two engine memory budgets were re-baselined on the national South Korea routing graph (188b65effcc6ef5c) and widened with it (idle 470 -> 1100 MiB, load peak 800 -> 2000 MiB), because engine RSS grows with the graph it loads. Applied to the Seoul graph those numbers would let a doubled Seoul RSS pass, so each engine MiB metric names the graph it was baselined on (baseline.routingGraphContentSha256) and evaluateBudget refuses (ENGINE_GRAPH_NOT_BASELINED) to judge it on samples from another graph or from a run that does not record its graph (details.routingGraph). engine.routeUnderLoadMs keeps its M2-01k-f (Seoul) baseline; it is a time budget and not graph-bound.

api.uploadParseMs.description: PUT of the 780 KB FIT through the production API: storage plus server re-parse in the bounded parse host (parse, normalize, map_path, aggregates). Since M2-01ai the parse runs in a child process, not a worker thread; the budget is unchanged.

headroom.reason: Timing on a shared 8-CPU machine whose 1-minute load average stayed around 3-4x the CPU count while the baseline was taken; per-run p95 moved by up to ~40 % between baseline runs. 2x keeps a judged run on the same machine from failing on load alone while still failing a regression that doubles the path.

api.finalizeMs.description: Finalize of the stored track (derivatives committed).

headroom.reason: An operation of a few milliseconds is the same order as one GC pause or scheduler delay on the loaded machine, so a 2x factor would fail on noise alone; 5x (tens of milliseconds) still fails a regression that turns the read into real work, e.g. re-deriving the artifact per request.

api.processPeakRssMiB.description: Peak RSS of the process hosting the API (includes the probe itself and the synthetic FIT generator). Since M2-01ai each parse runs in a child process, so parse memory is not in this number; it is budgeted separately as worker.parseProcessPeakRssMiB. M2-01aj re-derived this budget from three record-only runs of the child-process parser: the earlier baseline (716 MiB, budget 1,100) was taken while the parse workers were threads of this process, and that budget would have let this process grow 2.1x before failing.

headroom.reason: Resident and heap memory move with GC timing and allocator behaviour, not with machine load; 1.5x admits that jitter and fails a regression that holds half again as much.

engine.idleRssMiB.description: GraphHopper JVM RSS after one warm-up route, before load (-Xms512m -Xmx2048m). Bound to that graph: runs on any other graph are refused, not judged.

worker.minimumHeapCeilingMiB.description: Smallest V8 old-generation ceiling under which the long track parses (--max-old-space-size of the parse process since M2-01ai; worker resourceLimits before); below it V8 ends the parse process with TRACK_PARSE_MEMORY_EXCEEDED.

headroom.reason: The smallest ceiling is read off a discrete ladder (16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, ...); 2x is the next rung pair up and stays far below the product ceiling of 256 MiB.

worker.parseProcessPeakRssMiB.description: Peak RSS of one parse process (M2-01aj): the child process a bounded parser forks for each parse (default 256 MiB old-generation ceiling), read with ps every 20 ms while it parses the long track, one parse at a time, in parses separate from the worker.parseMs samples. A reading can miss a peak shorter than the interval, so a sample is a lower bound of the true peak; the baseline was read the same way. An API runs at most four of these processes at once (two parsers, concurrency 2 each).
